questions.q: To obtain a real estate salesperson license, a person typically must:
o: complete pre-licensing education and pass a state exam
questions.x: Licensing is regulated by each state.

questions.q: Real estate licenses are issued by:
o: state real estate commissions or licensing boards
questions.x: Each state regulates licensing.

questions.q: An encroachment occurs when:
o: a structure extends onto a neighbor's property
questions.x: A fence or garage over the lot line is an encroachment.

questions.q: Air rights give the owner the right to:
o: use the space above the land
questions.x: Air rights can be sold, for example to allow taller buildings.

questions.q: A mortgage banker or loan officer primarily:
o: originates and funds loans for real estate purchases
questions.x: Mortgage professionals finance real estate.

questions.q: Appurtenances are:
o: rights or privileges that belong to and pass with the property
questions.x: Examples include easements and water rights.

questions.q: Depreciation in real estate appraisal refers to:
o: a loss in value from any cause, such as wear or obsolescence
questions.x: Physical, functional, and external obsolescence reduce value.

questions.q: A chandelier permanently wired into a ceiling is generally considered a:
o: trade fixture that leaves with the tenant
fixture, and part of the real property
questions.x: Fixtures are attached items that convey with the property unless excluded.

questions.q: Market value is:
o: the most probable price a property would bring in a competitive, open market
questions.x: Market value assumes informed, willing buyers and sellers.

questions.q: Hereditaments are:
o: any property, real or personal, that can be inherited
questions.x: The term refers to inheritable property.

questions.q: An easement is:
o: the right to use another person's land for a specific purpose
questions.x: For example, a utility company's right to run lines across a lot.

questions.q: Real property includes:
o: land and anything permanently attached to it
questions.x: Real property is land plus permanent improvements and attached rights.

questions.q: Warehouses and manufacturing plants are classified as:
questions.x: Industrial property supports production, storage, and distribution.

questions.q: A REALTOR® is a real estate professional who:
o: is a member of the National Association of REALTORS® and follows its Code of Ethics
works only in commercial real estate
questions.x: 'REALTOR' is a registered trademark for NAR members.

questions.q: Comparable properties in an appraisal are:
o: any property with the same color
recently sold properties similar to the subject property
properties for sale in another state
questions.x: Comps are adjusted for differences in features.

questions.q: The sales comparison approach to valuation uses:
o: the cost to rebuild the structure
questions.x: It is the most common approach for homes.

questions.q: A home inspector's role differs from an appraiser's because an inspector:
o: sets the property's market value for the lender
evaluates the property's physical condition and systems
questions.x: Inspectors look for defects; appraisers estimate value.

questions.q: Which is a characteristic that makes land unique as an asset?
o: It loses all value every year
questions.x: Immobility, indestructibility, and uniqueness are physical characteristics of land.

questions.q: An appraisal is:
o: an unbiased professional estimate of a property's market value
questions.x: Lenders require appraisals to support loan amounts.

questions.q: The cost approach estimates value by:
o: adding land value to the cost of replacing the structure, minus depreciation
questions.x: It is useful for new or special-purpose buildings.

questions.q: Which is an example of commercial real estate?
o: A duplex where the owner lives
A vacation cabin for personal use
questions.x: Commercial real estate generates business income: offices, retail, industrial.

questions.q: The highest and best use of a property is the use that is:
o: legally permitted, physically possible, financially feasible, and most profitable
the use the current owner prefers
questions.x: Appraisers consider highest and best use when valuing property.

questions.q: A real estate entrepreneur, such as an investor or developer, typically:
o: identifies opportunities, takes financial risk, and adds value to property
works only as a salaried government employee
questions.x: Developers buy land, build, renovate, or reposition properties for profit.

questions.q: The income approach to valuation is most often used for:
questions.x: Value is based on the income the property generates.

questions.q: A leasing agent primarily:
o: finds tenants and negotiates leases for rental properties
questions.x: Leasing agents market vacancies and sign tenants.

questions.q: A multiple listing service (MLS) is:
o: a database where brokers share property listings
questions.x: MLS enables cooperation among brokers.

questions.q: Land use refers to:
o: the number of real estate agents
how land is utilized, such as residential, commercial, agricultural, or recreational
questions.x: Land use is shaped by zoning, markets, and planning.

questions.q: A mechanic's lien may be filed by:
o: a contractor who was not paid for work on the property
questions.x: It secures payment for labor or materials.

questions.q: The difference between a real estate agent and a broker is that a broker:
o: has additional education and licensing and may operate a brokerage and supervise agents
questions.x: Agents (salespersons) must work under a licensed broker.

questions.q: Mixed-use property combines:
o: residential, commercial, and/or other uses in one development
questions.x: Example: apartments above ground-floor retail.

questions.q: A lien is:
o: a legal claim against property as security for a debt
questions.x: Mortgages, tax liens, and mechanic's liens are examples.

questions.q: Real estate continuing education is required to:
o: keep a license active and stay current on laws and practices
questions.x: Most states require CE for license renewal.

questions.q: Trade fixtures are items that:
o: a business tenant installs for its business and may remove when the lease ends
questions.x: Trade fixtures remain the tenant's personal property.

questions.q: Personal property is best described as:
o: movable items not permanently attached to land
questions.x: Personal property (chattels) is movable.

questions.q: A benefit of membership in the National Association of REALTORS® is:
o: access to professional resources, education, and the right to use the REALTOR® trademark
questions.x: Members also must follow NAR's Code of Ethics.

questions.q: A property manager's main responsibility is to:
o: oversee the daily operation of rental properties for the owner
questions.x: Property managers handle tenants, rent collection, and maintenance.

questions.q: Fiduciary duties owed by an agent to a client include:
o: sharing the client's secrets with the other party
loyalty, obedience, confidentiality, disclosure, accounting, and reasonable care
questions.x: Often remembered by the acronym OLD CAR.

questions.q: Familial status as a protected class protects:
o: households with children under 18 and pregnant women
questions.x: Landlords generally cannot refuse renters because they have children.

questions.q: Escheat occurs when:
o: property reverts to the state because the owner died without a will or heirs
questions.x: Escheat ensures property is not left ownerless.

questions.q: Property taxes are typically assessed by:
questions.x: Counties, municipalities, and school districts levy property taxes.

questions.q: A security deposit is collected by a landlord to:
o: cover unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear
questions.x: State laws regulate how deposits are held and returned.

questions.q: A periodic tenancy, such as month-to-month, is one that:
o: automatically renews for successive periods until notice is given
questions.x: Either party may end it with proper notice.

questions.q: An advertisement that says 'adults only, no children' for a regular apartment complex likely violates:
o: the Fair Housing Act's protection of familial status
questions.x: Housing for older persons is a limited exception.

questions.q: Zoning laws regulate:
o: the interest rate on a mortgage
how land in specific areas may be used
questions.x: Zoning divides land into residential, commercial, industrial, and other districts.

questions.q: Eminent domain is the government's right to:
o: take private property for public use with just compensation
questions.x: The Fifth Amendment requires just compensation.

questions.q: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) plays a role in real estate by:
o: regulating mortgage lending practices to protect consumers
questions.x: The CFPB enforces TILA-RESPA rules.

questions.q: A variance is:
o: permission to use property in a way that does not strictly comply with zoning rules
questions.x: Variances are granted for hardships.

questions.q: Blockbusting is the illegal practice of:
o: persuading owners to sell by claiming people of a protected class are moving into the area
questions.x: Blockbusting exploits fear for profit.

questions.q: In a lease, the tenant is called the:
questions.x: The lessor is the landlord.

questions.q: Asbestos is a concern in older buildings because:
o: it is a type of insulation that improves value
its fibers can cause serious lung disease when disturbed
questions.x: Disclosure and proper abatement protect occupants.

questions.q: The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) protects buyers by:
o: requiring disclosure of settlement costs and prohibiting kickbacks
questions.x: RESPA covers federally related mortgage loans.

questions.q: The federal Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on:
o: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, and disability
questions.x: These are the seven federally protected classes.

questions.q: Which is a protected class under the federal Fair Housing Act?
questions.x: Disability (handicap) is one of the seven federally protected classes.

questions.q: The Truth in Lending Act (TILA) requires lenders to disclose:
o: the APR and total cost of credit
questions.x: TILA promotes informed use of consumer credit.

questions.q: The Americans with Disabilities Act affects real estate mainly by requiring:
o: accessibility in commercial properties and public accommodations
questions.x: Fair Housing Act rules cover accessibility in multifamily housing.

questions.q: Eviction is the legal process of:
o: removing a tenant from a rental property
questions.x: Landlords must follow court procedures.

questions.q: Building codes establish:
questions.x: Codes cover structure, electrical, plumbing, and fire safety.

questions.q: Steering is an illegal practice in which an agent:
o: gives buyers a list of all listings
guides buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on a protected class
questions.x: Steering limits housing choices and violates fair housing law.

questions.q: The Closing Disclosure must be provided to the borrower at least how many business days before closing?
questions.x: The TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule requires 3 business days.

questions.q: Sellers of homes built before 1978 must disclose known information about:
questions.x: Federal law requires lead-based paint disclosure for pre-1978 housing.

questions.q: State real estate commissions are responsible for:
o: licensing agents and enforcing real estate laws
questions.x: Commissions regulate licensee conduct.

questions.q: HOA covenants (CC&Rs) are:
o: private restrictions on how property in a community may be used
questions.x: Covenants, conditions, and restrictions bind owners in the community.

questions.q: Redlining is the illegal practice of:
o: refusing loans or insurance in certain areas based on the residents' race or ethnicity
marking up contracts in red ink
questions.x: Redlining denies services to neighborhoods based on protected characteristics.

questions.q: A nonconforming use is:
o: an illegal use that must stop today
a use that was legal before a zoning change and is allowed to continue
questions.x: It is 'grandfathered' under the new zoning.

questions.q: A lease is:
o: a contract granting a tenant the right to occupy property for a period in exchange for rent
questions.x: The landlord is the lessor; the tenant is the lessee.

questions.q: An adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) has an interest rate that:
o: can change periodically based on an index
questions.x: ARMs often start lower but carry rate risk.

questions.q: A deed is:
o: a written document that transfers ownership (title) of real property
questions.x: The grantor conveys title to the grantee.

questions.q: Closing (settlement) is the step in which:
o: documents are signed, funds are disbursed, and ownership transfers to the buyer
questions.x: After closing, the deed is recorded.

questions.q: The secondary mortgage market is where:
o: homes are sold for the second time
existing mortgages are bought and sold by investors such as Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
questions.x: It provides liquidity so lenders can make more loans.

questions.q: A fixed-rate mortgage has:
o: an interest rate that stays the same for the life of the loan
an interest rate that changes periodically
questions.x: Payments for principal and interest remain constant.

questions.q: A real estate investment trust (REIT) allows investors to:
o: invest in a portfolio of income-producing real estate through shares
buy land directly from the government
questions.x: REITs pay most of their taxable income as dividends.

questions.q: Title insurance protects the buyer and lender against:
o: losses from defects in the title, such as undiscovered liens
questions.x: A title search reduces but does not eliminate risk.

questions.q: A contingency in a purchase contract is:
o: a condition that must be met for the contract to proceed, such as financing or inspection
questions.x: Contingencies protect buyers or sellers.

questions.q: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is usually required when:
o: a conventional loan's down payment is less than 20%
questions.x: PMI protects the lender, not the borrower.

questions.q: A rental property earns $24,000 in net operating income and is valued at $300,000. What is its capitalization (cap) rate?
questions.x: Cap rate = NOI ÷ value = 24,000 ÷ 300,000 = 8%.

questions.q: A buyer purchases a $300,000 home with a 20% down payment. What is the loan amount?
The loan-to-value (LTV) ratio compares:
o: the loan amount with the property's appraised value
questions.x: LTV = loan ÷ value; lower LTV means less lender risk.

questions.q: Escrow is:
o: a neutral third party holding funds and documents until conditions of the sale are met
questions.x: Escrow ensures neither party is cheated.

questions.q: Foreclosure is:
o: the legal process by which a lender takes property after the borrower defaults
questions.x: Foreclosure lets the lender recover the loan balance.

questions.q: A VA loan is available to:
questions.x: VA loans are guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs.

questions.q: Recording a deed in the county records:
questions.x: Recording protects the new owner's interest.

questions.q: Earnest money is:
o: a deposit made by the buyer to show good faith when making an offer
questions.x: It is usually held in escrow and applied at closing.

questions.q: Cash flow from a rental property equals:
o: rental income minus operating expenses and debt payments
questions.x: Positive cash flow means income exceeds expenses.

questions.q: A quitclaim deed:
o: transfers whatever interest the grantor has, with no warranties
questions.x: Quitclaims are often used between family members or to clear title issues.

questions.q: Closing costs may include:
o: loan origination fees, title insurance, and recording fees
questions.x: Closing costs are typically 2–5% of the loan amount.

questions.q: An FHA loan is a mortgage that is:
o: insured by the Federal Housing Administration, allowing lower down payments
questions.x: FHA loans help first-time and lower-credit buyers.

questions.q: A mortgage is:
o: a loan secured by real property
questions.x: If the borrower defaults, the lender can foreclose.

questions.q: A general warranty deed provides the buyer with:
o: the greatest protection, guaranteeing clear title against all claims
questions.x: The grantor warrants title against defects from any time.

questions.q: The typical order of a home purchase transaction is:
o: offer, acceptance, inspection and appraisal, financing approval, closing
questions.x: Contingencies are resolved before closing.

questions.q: Truth in advertising in real estate requires that ads:
o: accurately describe the property and not mislead buyers
questions.x: Misrepresentation can violate license law and consumer protection laws.

questions.q: An agent who knowingly hides a leaking roof from buyers is guilty of:
questions.x: Agents must disclose known material defects.

questions.q: Which is an ethical violation by an agent?
o: Presenting all offers to the seller
Accepting an undisclosed kickback from a lender
questions.x: Undisclosed kickbacks also violate RESPA.

questions.q: The NAR Code of Ethics requires REALTORS® to:
o: protect and promote clients' interests while treating all parties honestly
questions.x: Article 1 addresses duties to clients and honesty to all parties.

questions.q: 'Puffing' in real estate refers to:
o: exaggerated opinions, such as 'best view in town,' that are not statements of fact
questions.x: Puffing is generally legal; false statements of fact are not.

questions.q: An agent must present to the seller:
o: all written offers in a timely manner
no offers until the home is inspected
only offers from the agent's own clients
questions.x: Sellers decide which offers to accept.

questions.q: An agency relationship is created when:
o: a principal authorizes an agent to act on their behalf
a buyer looks at a website
questions.x: The client (principal) relies on the agent's loyalty and expertise.

questions.q: Staging a home before listing means:
o: arranging furniture and decor to make the home appealing to buyers
questions.x: Staged homes often photograph and sell better.

questions.q: A 'for sale by owner' (FSBO) property is one where:
o: the owner sells without a listing agent
questions.x: FSBO sellers save commission but handle marketing and negotiation.

questions.q: Dual agency occurs when:
o: one agent or brokerage represents both the buyer and seller in the same transaction
an agent works for two companies
questions.x: Dual agency requires informed written consent where it is legal.

questions.q: A home sells for $400,000 with a 5% total commission. What is the total commission?
Agents must disclose their agency relationship to consumers in order to:
o: make clear whose interests the agent represents
questions.x: Agency disclosure laws protect consumers.

questions.q: An exclusive right-to-sell listing means:
o: the seller can sell it alone without paying a commission
the broker earns a commission no matter who sells the property during the listing period
questions.x: It is the most common listing type.

questions.q: A buyer representation agreement is signed between:
o: a buyer and a buyer's broker
questions.x: It formalizes the buyer agency relationship.

questions.q: A buyer's agent represents:
o: the buyer's interests in a transaction
questions.x: Buyer's agents help clients find and negotiate for property.

questions.q: A real estate sales agent's responsibilities include:
o: marketing listings, showing properties, and negotiating offers
questions.x: Agents guide clients through transactions.

questions.q: Agents in residential transactions typically work with:
o: individuals and families buying or selling homes
questions.x: Residential agency centers on homeowners.

questions.q: A subagent is:
o: an agent from another brokerage who works on behalf of the listing broker's client
questions.x: Subagents owe duties to the seller.

questions.q: Confidentiality as a fiduciary duty means an agent should not reveal:
o: the client's private information, such as the lowest price a seller will accept
questions.x: Material facts must still be disclosed to all parties.

questions.q: An open listing allows the seller to:
o: list with multiple brokers and pay only the broker who sells it
questions.x: Open listings are non-exclusive.

questions.q: A comparative market analysis (CMA) is prepared by an agent to:
o: replace an appraisal for a lender
help a seller choose a listing price based on similar properties
questions.x: A CMA is an agent's pricing tool, not a formal appraisal.

questions.q: The accounting duty requires an agent to:
o: safeguard and account for all money and property entrusted by the client
questions.x: Commingling client funds with personal funds is prohibited.

questions.q: In commercial real estate transactions, agents typically:
o: focus on income potential, leases, and investment analysis
questions.x: Commercial deals emphasize cash flow, cap rates, and lease terms.

questions.q: An open house is used to:
o: allow many potential buyers to view a property during a set time
questions.x: Open houses generate interest and leads.

questions.q: A commission in real estate is:
o: a fee paid to the brokerage, usually a percentage of the sale price
questions.x: Commissions are negotiable.

questions.q: A common way to advertise a property listing is:
o: online listing platforms, the MLS, and virtual tours
questions.x: Digital marketing reaches the most buyers.

questions.q: A seller's agent (listing agent) represents:
o: both parties equally in all cases
questions.x: Listing agents market the property and negotiate for the seller.

questions.q: A listing agreement is a contract between:
o: a property owner and a broker to market the property
questions.x: It sets the commission, term, and listing price.

questions.q: Which duty requires an agent to follow a client's lawful instructions?
questions.x: Agents must obey lawful instructions.
